title: Scientific Opinion on the re-evaluation of aspartame (E 951) as a food additive
authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS)
funder: European Food Safety Authority; on request from the European Commission (question number EFSA-Q-2011-00406).
result: Aspartame is rapidly and completely hydrolysed in the gastrointestinal tract to phenylalanine, aspartic acid and methanol. Developmental toxicity in animals was attributed to phenylalanine. The acceptable daily intake of 40 mg/kg bw per day was retained; in normal people and PKU heterozygotes, intakes up to the ADI in addition to dietary phenylalanine would not raise peak plasma phenylalanine above the clinical guideline for preventing adverse effects in fetuses. The ADI is not applicable to PKU patients.
